name: The Patel house and clinic
status: Canon 2 (address, "Patel house and clinic"); design interpreted from reference/board-23.jpg
style: Craftsman / Prairie foursquare with a one-story clinic wing
materials: dark red-brown brick ground floor, porch piers, knee walls, chimney and clinic wing
painted cedar shingles above the belt course, muted olive-khaki
cream painted trim, wide flat casings, brackets, tapered porch columns
stained oak doors with glazed tops
concrete porch floor and walks, asphalt clinic parking court
notes: House 12.6 x 12.0 m, two stories, low hip roof (25 deg) with 0.78 m eaves, ridge 9.5 m (Atlas height 7.5 m; within the 30% allowance). From board-23: the brick ground floor, deep hipped eaves, the front gable dormer with three windows, the wide porch on brick piers with a low gable over the steps, the stair-landing window, the stepped walk with clipped boxwood globes and landscape boulders, the big shade tree. Per the brief: shingles above the belt course (the photo is brick throughout), tapered columns on the piers, and the clinic wing on the right: one story, its own stoop under a small gable on tapered posts, a 1:12 ramp with steel rails, a blank bronze plaque (no text) by the door, and three striped parking stalls with wheel stops off a paved court that meets the curb. Interpreted: side and rear elevations, rear doors, the exterior chimney, beds and props. No fence or hedge on the frontage.
